intro: Covers the US session of Wednesday 18 November (and the ASX session of the same day). This is the 08:15 retry; an earlier 07:15 attempt was deferred because closing prints and SPI figures were unconfirmed. Caveats on reconciled figures are in the footnotes.
footnotes: US index closes from CNBC (updated 4:13pm ET), cross-checked against Yahoo Finance; VIX and US 10-year yield from Yahoo Finance and Trading Economics (10-year change -4bp to -5bp across sources; -5bp shown).
Brent: Trading Economics 91.84 (-1.83%) used; CNBC showed about US$90.83 in the afternoon. Gold, AUD/USD and Brent are CFD-based reference prices.
Iron ore print is dated 17 November (Trading Economics); no 18 November print was available.
SPI 200 futures: sources agree on level (about 8,787) and direction but differ on the change (-0.53% TradingView, -0.84% Investing.com); midpoint shown.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures were around 8,787 (Dec contract), down roughly 0.5-0.8% (TradingView -0.53%, Investing.com -0.84%; midpoint -0.69% used). Applied to the prior ASX 200 close of about 8,822 (-0.69% on Wednesday, a two-week low), that implies an open about 61 points (0.69%) lower, near 8,761. Trading Economics' ASX 200 table showed a conflicting 8,744; the 8,822 figure matches its news text and the -0.7% headline.

local_events: ABS October labour force (jobs) data, due today per Trading Economics; release time not verified
RBA speeches and other local data: none verified for today
what_moved: US stocks closed mixed as hawkish Fed minutes and a hot-inflation backdrop outweighed Nvidia's earnings beat: the Dow fell 1.11% and the S&P 500 slipped 0.23% for a fifth straight loss, while the Nasdaq rose 0.42%. Energy was the weakest S&P 500 sector, down nearly 3% as oil fell, and healthcare dragged the Dow; a full sector table was not available. Gold dropped more than 3% to its lowest since September 2025 on a firmer US dollar and rate-hike pricing, and AUD/USD fell to its weakest since January.

news.headline: Fed minutes point to further rate hikes
news.summary: Minutes of the October FOMC meeting showed almost all participants judged further tightening would likely be appropriate, with some favouring a 25bp hike in October and AI demand flagged as a material source of inflation risk.

news.headline: Waller floats half-point December hike
news.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50bp increase at the 8-9 December meeting is "probably necessary"; CME FedWatch put the odds of a 50bp cumulative move by end-January at about 69%.

news.headline: Gold slides to lowest since September 2025
news.summary: Spot gold fell more than 3% below US$3,800/oz on a firmer US dollar and rising Fed hike expectations.

news.headline: Nvidia beats but shares close lower
news.summary: Third-quarter revenue rose 103% year on year and guidance was lifted, yet the shares closed 2.9% lower amid CEO leadership turmoil, a delayed 10-Q filing and a reported SEC probe, weighing on AI-linked stocks.

news.headline: S&P 500 posts fifth straight loss as energy sinks
news.summary: The index fell for a fifth session, its longest losing run since June; the energy sector dropped nearly 3% as oil slid, and a UnitedHealth slump dragged the Dow to a session low.

news.headline: Anthropic IPO set to price, trading Thursday
news.summary: The AI developer was expected to price at US$70-78 a share (US$1.3-1.45 trillion valuation) with trading starting Thursday in New York.

news.headline: ASX 200 at two-week low; Australian dollar weakest since January
news.summary: The ASX 200 fell about 0.7% on Wednesday to a two-week low, and AUD/USD slipped to 0.671, its weakest level since mid-January.

news.headline: Bank Indonesia hikes; UK inflation at 3.6%
news.summary: Bank Indonesia delivered a surprise 25bp hike to 6%, and UK CPI printed at 3.6%, adding to the global tightening backdrop.

coming_up: Thursday 19 November: Anthropic begins trading in New York and US-China leader talks are due at APEC in Shenzhen. Next major macro event: the FOMC meeting on 8-9 December, where a 50bp hike has been floated.
